record.paper_title: Periods of Integrals on Algebraic Manifolds: Summary of Main Results and Discussion of Open Problems
record.original_question: Find methods for proving or disproving local Torelli theorems for algebraic varieties, where the local Torelli problem asks whether the Hodge structure on the cohomology of a fiber separates points in its local moduli (Kuranishi) space. In particular, determine whether the local Torelli theorem is true or false for simply connected canonical surfaces, meaning surfaces with ample canonical bundle.

evidence.quote: The local Torelli problem is the question of deciding when the Hodge structure on 2J*(F8, C) separates points in the local moduli space
Find methods to treat the local Torelli theorem. In particular, decide whether it is true or false for simply-connected canonical surfaces

artifact.category_tag: Local Torelli for surfaces of general type
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a smooth complex projective variety, and let {X_s : s ∈ S} → S be the Kuranishi (local versal) deformation of X, where S is a germ of the local moduli space at the point 0 corresponding to X. For each s ∈ S the complex cohomology H^k(X_s, C) carries a pure Hodge structure of weight k, given by the Hodge filtration F^p H^k(X_s, C). The local period map sends s ∈ S to the point in the appropriate flag variety (period domain) parametrising this Hodge filtration on the fixed underlying vector space H^k(X, C) (identified via the Gauss–Manin connection).

The local Torelli problem asks whether this local period map is injective (equivalently, whether the Hodge structures on the cohomology of the fibers separate points of S near 0).

(a) Develop general methods, applicable to broad classes of smooth projective varieties, by which the local Torelli theorem can be either established or refuted.

(b) Determine whether the local Torelli theorem holds for every simply connected smooth complex projective surface X with ample canonical bundle K_X (i.e. a simply connected canonical surface of general type): that is, decide whether for every such X the local period map on its Kuranishi space is injective at 0, or exhibit a counterexample.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is partially resolved. Kynev (1977) constructed a simply connected surface of general type (a "Kunev surface", with p_g = 1, K^2 = 1) for which the local/infinitesimal Torelli theorem fails; this gives a negative answer for general simply connected canonical surfaces. Catanese and Todorov subsequently produced families with K ample violating global Torelli. The broader question of finding general methods/criteria for local Torelli, and of classifying exactly which canonical surfaces satisfy local Torelli, remains an active area of research.
